# Workcell

Use Workcell only when concurrent commands contend for the same named, host-local resource, such as a device, VM, GPU, port, generated artifact, or license seat. Prefer a project’s checked-in wrapper and resource key. Do not invent a key or wrap a command that already uses Workcell.

```text
workcell run <resource> [--wait] [--session <id>] [--json] -- <command...>
workcell status <resource> [--json]
```

Use `--json`. A completed result includes the wrapped exit code and `log_path`. A busy non-waiting run exits `75` without running the command and supplies `next_action.wait_argv`; execute that unchanged only when the result is still needed, or continue unrelated work.

Never poll, bypass the queue, terminate its owner, or manually nest reservations. Commands needing several resources must use a checked-in wrapper that acquires each key once in bytewise order. Workcell rejects same-key recursion and order inversion.

Workcell coordinates cooperative callers sharing one host and state root. It is not authorization, discovery, preemption, scheduling, or distributed locking.
